translation_en: Ali narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us. Amr said: Ata narrated to us, who said: The Prophet delayed the night prayer. Umar came and said, “Prayer, Messenger of Allah! The women and children have gone to sleep.” He came out with his head dripping with water and said: “Were it not that I would make things difficult for my community—or the people; Sufyan also said, ‘my community’—I would have ordered them to pray at this time.” Ibn Jurayj reported from Ata, from Ibn Abbas: The Prophet delayed this prayer. Umar came and said, “Messenger of Allah, the women and children have gone to sleep.” He came out wiping the water from his side and said: “This is its proper time, were it not that I would make things difficult for my community.” Amr reported from Ata without mentioning Ibn Abbas. Amr said, “His head was dripping,” while Ibn Jurayj said, “He was wiping water from his side.” Amr reported the wording, “Were it not that I would make things difficult for my community,” while Ibn Jurayj reported, “This is its proper time, were it not that I would make things difficult for my community.” Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us; Maan narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Amr, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet.

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Jafar ibn Rabiah, from Abd al-Rahman, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, say that the Messenger of Allah said: “Were it not that I would make things difficult for my community, I would have ordered them to use the tooth-stick.”

Ayyash ibn al-Walid narrated to us; Abd al-Ala narrated to us; Humayd narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet continued fasting without breaking the fast near the end of the month, and some people did the same. The Prophet heard about this and said: “If the month were extended for me, I would continue fasting in a way that would make those who go to extremes abandon their extremism. I am not like you; my Lord gives me food and drink.” Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah also reported this from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet.

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Al-Layth said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, that Said ibn al-Musayyab informed him that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah forbade continuous fasting. They said, “But you fast continuously.” He said: “Which of you is like me? I spend the night with my Lord giving me food and drink.” When they refused to stop, he fasted continuously with them for one day and then another. Then they saw the new moon, and he said: “If it had been delayed, I would have continued longer,” as a reprimand to them.

Musaddad narrated to us; Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us; Ashath narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, from Aishah, who said: I asked the Prophet, “Is the semicircular wall part of the House?” He said, “Yes.” I asked, “Then why did they not include it within the House?” He said: “Your people did not have enough funds.” I asked, “Why is its door raised?” He said: “Your people did that so they could let in whomever they wished and prevent whomever they wished. Were your people not so recently out of the Age of Ignorance, I would fear that their hearts would reject my including the wall within the House and bringing its door down to ground level.”

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us; Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “Were it not for the emigration, I would have been a man from the Ansar. If the people took one valley and the Ansar took another valley—or mountain pass—I would take the valley or pass of the Ansar.”

Musa narrated to us; Wuhayb narrated to us, from Amr ibn Yahya, from Abbad ibn Tamim, from Abdullah ibn Zayd, from the Prophet, who said: “Were it not for the emigration, I would have been a man from the Ansar. If the people took a valley or a mountain pass, I would take the valley of the Ansar and their mountain pass.” Abu al-Tayyah also reported it from Anas, from the Prophet, mentioning the mountain pass.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us; Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said: Malik told us: We came to the Prophet as young men of similar ages and stayed with him for twenty nights. The Messenger of Allah was gentle. When he thought that we longed for our families or missed them, he asked us about those we had left behind. We told him. He said: “Return to your families, stay with them, teach them and instruct them”—and he mentioned other things that I remember or may not remember—“and pray as you have seen me pray. When the time for prayer comes, let one of you call the prayer, and let the oldest among you lead you.”

Musaddad narrated to us, from Yahya, from al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman, from Ibn Masud, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “Let none of you be prevented by Bilal’s call to prayer from eating his pre-dawn meal. He calls—or announces—so that the one standing in prayer may return and the one sleeping may wake. Dawn is not when it appears like this”—and Yahya brought his palms together—“but when it appears like this.” Yahya spread apart his two index fingers.

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to us. He said: I heard Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, report from the Prophet, who said: “Bilal calls during the night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum calls.”

Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, who said: The Prophet led us in the noon prayer and prayed five units. He was told, “Has the prayer been increased?” He asked, “What is that?” They said, “You prayed five.” After giving the greeting, he performed two prostrations.

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah finished the prayer after two units. Dhu al-Yadayn said to him, “Messenger of Allah, has the prayer been shortened, or did you forget?” He said, “Has Dhu al-Yadayn spoken the truth?” The people said, “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah stood and prayed two more units, then gave the greeting. Then he said “Allahu akbar,” prostrated as long as—or longer than—his usual prostration, raised his head, said “Allahu akbar,” prostrated again as long as before, and then raised his head.

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: While the people were praying the dawn prayer at Quba, someone came to them and said: “Revelation of Quran came to the Messenger of Allah last night, and he has been ordered to face the Kaaba, so face it.” Their faces had been turned toward Syria, so they turned toward the Kaaba.

Yahya narrated to us; Waki narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara, who said: When the Messenger of Allah came to Madinah, he prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months. He wished to be directed toward the Kaaba, so Allah revealed: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah that pleases you” (2:144). He was then directed toward the Kaaba. A man prayed the afternoon prayer with him, then went out and passed by some of the Ansar, who were bowing in the afternoon prayer. He told them, bearing witness that he had prayed with the Prophet and that he had been directed toward the Kaaba. So they turned toward it while still bowing in the afternoon prayer.

Yahya ibn Qazah narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I was serving a drink made from dates to Abu Talhah al-Ansari, Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and Ubayy ibn Kab. Someone came to them and said, “Wine has been forbidden.” Abu Talhah said, “Anas, get up and break these jars.” Anas said: I got up, took a stone mortar of ours, and struck the jars with its bottom until they broke.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah, from Hudhayfah, that the Prophet said to the people of Najran: “I will send to you a man who is truly trustworthy.” The Companions of the Prophet looked eagerly for this distinction, and he sent Abu Ubaydah.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet said: “Every community has a trustworthy person, and the trustworthy person of this community is Abu Ubaydah.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Said, from Ubayd ibn Hunayn, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar, may Allah be pleased with them: There was a man from the Ansar who, whenever he was away from the Messenger of Allah while I was present, would bring me news of what had happened with the Messenger of Allah. Whenever I was away from the Messenger of Allah and he was present, he would bring me news of what had happened with the Messenger of Allah.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Ghundar narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Zubayd, from Sad ibn Ubaydah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet sent out an army and appointed a man over them. He lit a fire and said, “Enter it.” They intended to enter it, while others said, “We only fled from it.” They mentioned this to the Prophet. He said to those who intended to enter it: “Had you entered it, you would have remained in it until the Day of Resurrection.” He said to the others: “There is no obedience in disobedience; obedience is only in what is right.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us; Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, that Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah informed him that Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid informed him that two men brought a dispute to the Prophet.

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Masud informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah, a Bedouin stood and said, “Messenger of Allah, judge for me according to the Book of Allah.” His opponent stood and said, “He is right, Messenger of Allah; judge for him according to the Book of Allah, and allow me to speak.” The Prophet said, “Speak.” The man said: “My son worked for this man—an employee—and committed adultery with his wife. I was told that my son must be stoned, so I ransomed him with one hundred sheep and a slave girl. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they told me that his wife must be stoned, while my son must receive one hundred lashes and be exiled for one year.” The Prophet said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will judge between you according to the Book of Allah. The slave girl and sheep must be returned. Your son must receive one hundred lashes and be exiled for one year. And you, Unays”—he said this to a man from Aslam—“go tomorrow morning to this man’s wife; if she confesses, stone her.” Unays went to her the next morning. She confessed, and he stoned her.

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us; Ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: On the day of the Trench, the Prophet called for someone to volunteer, and al-Zubayr volunteered. He called them again, and al-Zubayr volunteered. He called them a third time, and al-Zubayr volunteered. He said: “Every prophet has a devoted disciple, and my devoted disciple is al-Zubayr.” Sufyan said: I memorized this from Ibn al-Munkadir. Ayyub said to him, “Abu Bakr, narrate to them from Jabir, for the people like hearing you narrate from Jabir.” In that gathering, he said, “I heard Jabir,” and continued to repeat, “I heard Jabir.” I asked Sufyan: “Al-Thawri says it was the day of Qurayzah.” He replied: “This is how I memorized it, just as you are sitting here: it was the day of the Trench.” Sufyan said, “It was one day,” and smiled.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Uthman, from Abu Musa: The Prophet entered a walled garden and ordered me to guard its gate. A man came asking permission to enter. He said, “Let him in and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.” It was Abu Bakr. Then Umar came, and he said, “Let him in and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.” Then Uthman came, and he said, “Let him in and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Yahya, from Ubayd ibn Hunayn, who heard Ibn Abbas narrate from Umar, may Allah be pleased with them: I came and found the Messenger of Allah in an upper room of his. A black servant of the Messenger of Allah was at the top of the stairs. I said, “Tell him this is Umar ibn al-Khattab.” He gave me permission to enter.

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah informed me that Abdullah ibn Abbas told him that the Messenger of Allah sent his letter to Khosrow and ordered that it be delivered to the governor of Bahrain, who would deliver it to Khosrow. When Khosrow read it, he tore it up. I think Ibn al-Musayyab said: The Messenger of Allah prayed that they be utterly torn apart.

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd; Salamah ibn al-Akwa narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah said to a man from Aslam: “Announce to your people—or to the people—on the day of Ashura: whoever has eaten should complete the rest of that day without eating, and whoever has not eaten should fast.”

Ali ibn al-Jad informed us; Shubah informed us. Ishaq narrated to me; al-Nadr informed us; Shubah informed us, from Abu Jamrah, who said: Ibn Abbas used to seat me on his couch and said: When the delegation of Abd al-Qays came to the Messenger of Allah, he asked, “Who are the people of the delegation?” They said, “Rabi’ah.” He said: “Welcome to the delegation and the people, arriving without disgrace or regret.” They said, “Messenger of Allah, between us and you are the unbelievers of Mudar. Tell us something by which we may enter Paradise and inform those behind us.” They asked him about drinks. He forbade them four containers and commanded them four things. He commanded them to believe in Allah and asked, “Do you know what belief in Allah is?” They said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “To testify that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; to establish prayer; to give zakah”—I think he also mentioned fasting Ramadan—“and to give one-fifth of the spoils.” He forbade them the gourd, the green jar, the pitch-coated vessel, and the hollowed-out log; perhaps he said the tarred vessel. He said: “Remember these instructions and convey them to those behind you.”

Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Tawbah al-Anbari, who said: Al-Shabi said to me: “What do you make of al-Hasan’s hadith from the Prophet?” I kept company with Ibn Umar for nearly two years—or a year and a half—and did not hear him narrate from the Prophet except this: Some Companions of the Prophet, including Sad, went to eat some meat. A woman from one of the Prophet’s wives called to them, “It is the meat of a lizard.” They stopped. The Messenger of Allah said: “Eat it—or eat from it—for it is lawful—or, he said, there is no harm in it; the narrator was uncertain—but it is not food I eat.”

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah said: “I was sent with concise, comprehensive speech, and I was aided by awe. While I was asleep, I saw that the keys to the treasures of the earth were brought to me and placed in my hand.” Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah has gone, while you are greedily enjoying them—or grazing on them, or a similar word.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Said, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “There was no prophet among the prophets who was not given signs like those through which people believed. What I was given is revelation that Allah revealed to me, and I hope that I will have the greatest number of followers on the Day of Resurrection.”
